events.title: Proposed ruling: no_action (model confidence 0.82)
events.body:
Gateway: the cancellation on record was made by the rider, so the fee can only be assessed through the rider-cancellation branch of NS-0 [F2][NS-0]. The timing is not in dispute: acceptance 21:30:00, rider cancellation 21:33:20, i.e. 3 min 20 s (200 s) after matching [F2]. That is more than 3 minutes, so the $6.61 fee is payable and NS-4 yields no_action [F2][F5][NS-4].

The rider's answer is that the no-show conditions in NS-1 were never met — no "I'm Here" tap, no recorded arrival, never within 200 m [F3][F4][F1]. Those facts are accepted as true, but NS-1 addresses the situation where the driver presses "I'm Here", waits over 3 minutes and cancels for rider no-show, with NS-2 as the sanction when those preconditions fail [F3][F4][NS-1]. Here no driver-side no-show was asserted and the driver did not cancel; the system trace records cancelled_by = rider, and the vehicle remained en route (closest approach 2501 m) [F1][F2][F3][F4][NS-1]. NS-2 therefore has no charge to reverse: it operates on a driver-cancelled no-show charge, which this is not [F2][F5][NS-2].

No flat-rate over-collection exists to refund under FARE-1: the recorded cancellation fee is exactly the published $6.61 with a 1.0× surge multiplier and no other add-on [F5][F6][FARE-1]. NS-6 (waiting fee) is also inapplicable, as no "I'm Here" tap and no waiting fee are on record [F4][F5][NS-6]. The rider's real grievance — cancelling because the driver was still 2501 m away while messaging "About 5 min, traffic" [F1][F7][F8] — is a service-quality argument, not a published ground for waiving the fee; the lateness-vs-ETA waiver is expressly informational (NS-8), and the traffic record (band 3 on Jalan Buroh, no incidents, fair weather) does not document a disruption on this route [F8][F10][F11][F12][NS-4]. The profile facts on both sides (clean rider record; 1081 driver trips, 0 upheld disputes) are noted but cannot decide the fee [F13][F14][NS-4]. No ground for an account flag arises: no abuse of the cancellation/waiting buttons is shown, and no RD-1 violation is recorded in this no-show matter [F4][F14][NS-3]. Amount payable: nil (fee stands).

points.response: Conceded on the arithmetic only: the rider cancelled at 21:33:20, 20 s past the 3-minute mark (F2), so on timing alone NS-4 would make the fee payable. But NS-4 is the rider-cancellation branch of the single gateway in NS-0, and it does not create a fee where the pickup no-show preconditions of NS-1 in the same section are unmet.

A flat charge at the published rate with 1.0x surge (F5, F6) shows only that the rate was not inflated; FARE-1 governs whether a charge is payable at all, and the $6.61 here rests entirely on NS-1's conditions being met, which the system records show they were not.

This is the point that decides the case, and the driver's concession destroys his own fee: the driver never tapped "I'm Here" (F4) and the platform never recorded arrival at the pickup (F3), so requirement (i) of NS-1 fails, and NS-2 mandates a full refund of the $6.61 whenever any NS-1 element is missing.

The driver's own chat promised arrival in "about 5 min, traffic" — roughly 21:36 (F8, F2) — while GPS puts his closest approach at 2501 m and he never entered 200 m of the pickup (F1), so he could not have been at the pickup location under NS-1(ii); the absence of an ETA-waiver rule does not create a charge that NS-1 and NS-2 withhold.

We did not request any account action against the driver in this case, so his trip volume and clean 90-day record (F14) are not in issue; the rider's own clean profile (F13) equally shows this claim is genuine, and neither profile fact can decide the case.

Conceded: the trip is an on-demand RydeX job and the rider's cancellation at 21:33:20 is 3 min 20 s after acceptance at 21:30:00, so on timing alone the $6.61 fee is payable under the rider-cancellation branch.
Conceded: driver_arrived_at is null, so the platform recorded no arrival at the pickup point and the driver presses no arrival claim here.

Accepted as to the GPS record (closest approach 2501 m, never within 200 m); but NS-1/NS-2 are the conditions for a driver-asserted rider no-show, and the driver never asserted a no-show — the charge in issue was triggered by the rider's own cancellation at 3 min 20 s, which is governed by NS-4.

The null driver_pressed_here_at (F4) means no waiting fee was or could be claimed and no NS-1 no-show was asserted by the driver; it does not by itself negate the rider-cancellation fee that NS-4 makes payable after 3 minutes.

The rider's own chat asked 'How long will you be?' (F7) and the driver answered 'About 5 min, traffic' (F8) — the rider chose to cancel before that estimate expired, and Ryde publishes no ETA-based waiver (NS-8 is informational and cannot ground the rider's claim), so the lateness narrative adds nothing to NS-4.

The traffic record confirms the delay was not documented congestion (F10 band 3 is non-severe and on Jalan Buroh, F11 no incidents, F12 fair weather), but NS-4 does not condition the fee on congestion — a driver being slowed is not a published free-cancellation ground, so this point does not defeat the fee.

NS-2 applies only where the driver cancelled or asserted a rider no-show without meeting NS-1 — neither happened here; the charge arose from the rider's cancellation 3 min 20 s after matching (F2, F5), so there is nothing to refund under NS-2/NS-7.

The rider's clean profile (F13) is not disputed, but profile facts cannot decide the fee; the same is true of the driver's 1081 trips and 0 upheld disputes (F14), so neither record changes the NS-4 outcome.
